```{r, include = FALSE}
# the full examples run when the package is built; CRAN checks skip them for time
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(bayescompR)
# chains run in parallel on this many cores; on your own machine use
# options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
options(mc.cores = 2)
```

CmdStan is a set of command line programs: `stanc` compiles and checks a
program, the compiled model samples, optimizes or approximates, and
`stansummary` and `diagnose` read the CSV files it writes. bayescompR
offers every step as an R function that reads and writes the same files,
so a project can move between CmdStan, CmdStanR and bayescompR, or mix
them. This vignette follows one model through that workflow.

| CmdStan or stanc | bayescompR |
|---|---|
| `stanc --version` | `bayescomp_stan_version()` |
| `stanc` (type check) | `bayescomp_check()` |
| `stanc --info` | `bayescomp_info()` |
| `stanc --auto-format`, `--canonicalize` | `bayescomp_format()` |
| `stanc --warn-pedantic`, `--warn-uninitialized` | `bayescomp_pedantic()`, `bayescomp_uninitialized()` |
| `stanc --standalone-functions` | `bayescomp_expose_functions()` |
| `stanc --debug-generate-data`, `--debug-generate-inits` | `bayescomp_generate_data()`, `bayescomp_generate_inits()` |
| JSON and R dump data files | `bayescomp_read_data()`, `bayescomp_write_data()` |
| `model sample` | `bayescomp_sample()` |
| `model optimize`, `laplace`, `pathfinder`, `variational` | `bayescomp_optimize()`, `bayescomp_laplace()`, `bayescomp_pathfinder()`, `bayescomp_variational()` |
| `model generate_quantities` | `bayescomp_generate_quantities()` |
| `model log_prob` | `bayescomp_log_prob()`, `bayescomp_grad_log_prob()` |
| `model diagnose` (gradient test) | `bayescomp_check_gradients()` |
| `output.csv`, `metric_file`, `diagnostic_file`, `profile_file` | `bayescomp_write_csv()`, `bayescomp_read_csv()` |
| `bin/stansummary` | `bayescomp_stansummary()` |
| `bin/diagnose` | `bayescomp_diagnose()` |

## Checking a program

```{r}
code <- "
functions {
  real scaled_logit(real p, real s) {
    return s * logit(p);
  }
}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  array[N] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;
  vector[N] x;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  real beta;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, 2.5);
  beta ~ normal(0, 2.5);
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha + beta * x);
}
generated quantities {
  real p_mean = inv_logit(alpha);
}
"
bayescomp_stan_version()
bayescomp_check(code)
```

`bayescomp_info()` lists what stanc's `--info` reports: the data,
parameters and generated quantities with their types and sizes, the
library functions and the distributions the program uses.

```{r}
str(bayescomp_info(code), max.level = 1)
bayescomp_info(code)$parameters$alpha
```

`bayescomp_format()` prints a program in stanc's canonical layout,
breaking lines longer than `max_line_length`. `canonicalize`, as stanc's
`--canonicalize`, also drops redundant parentheses (`"parentheses"`), puts
braces around the bodies of `if`, `for` and `while` (`"braces"`) and
inlines `#include` files (`"includes"`); `TRUE` does all of them.

```{r}
cat(bayescomp_format("parameters{real mu;}model{mu~normal(0,1);}"))
cat(bayescomp_format("parameters{real mu;}model{if ((mu) > 0) mu~normal((0),1);}", canonicalize = TRUE))
```

`bayescomp_check()` type checks a program as stanc does, signals an
error for an invalid one and invisibly returns the typed program;
`pedantic = TRUE` and `warn_uninitialized = TRUE` also print the warnings
described next.

The pedantic mode warns about programs that are legal but probably not
what was meant: parameters without priors, priors with very wide scales,
integer division, control flow that depends on parameters and variables
that may be used before they are assigned.

```{r}
bayescomp_pedantic("data { int N; } parameters { real mu; real<lower=0> s; }
                    model { mu ~ normal(0, 1000); }")
bayescomp_uninitialized("parameters { real mu; } model { real a; mu ~ normal(a, 1); }")
```

## Data files

CmdStan reads data and initial values from JSON or R dump files.
`bayescomp_write_data()` writes JSON with the conventions CmdStan expects
(integers stay integers, arrays and matrices are nested row major, and
infinite values are written as `"Infinity"` and `"-Infinity"`, `NaN` as
`"NaN"` and `NA` as `null`), and
`bayescomp_read_data()` reads either format back. `bayescomp_model()` and
the `init` argument of the samplers accept a file name directly.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
N <- 100
x <- rnorm(N)
dat <- list(N = N, y = rbinom(N, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 1.2 * x)), x = x)
data_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
bayescomp_write_data(dat, data_file)
str(bayescomp_read_data(data_file))
model <- bayescomp_model(code, data = data_file)
model
```

For testing a program before real data exist, stanc can generate random
data and initial values that satisfy the declared constraints:

```{r}
str(bayescomp_generate_data(code, seed = 1))
str(bayescomp_generate_inits(model, seed = 1))
```

## Functions from the program

`bayescomp_expose_functions()` returns the functions block as R functions,
which helps to test them on their own:

```{r}
f <- bayescomp_expose_functions(model)
f$scaled_logit(0.75, 2)
```

## The gradient test

CmdStan's `diagnose` method compares the gradient of the log density with
finite differences at an initial point. A large error points to a bug in
the program or in the library.

```{r}
bayescomp_check_gradients(model, seed = 1)
```

## Running and writing CSV files

```{r}
fit <- bayescomp_sample(model, chains = 2, iter_warmup = 500, iter_sampling = 500,
                        seed = 123, refresh = 0)
out_dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(out_dir)
files <- bayescomp_write_csv(fit, out_dir, basename = "logistic",
                             save_metric = TRUE, save_config = TRUE)
basename(files)
list.files(out_dir)
```

The CSV files have CmdStan's comment header (configuration, adaptation
results, step size and metric, timing), one column per flattened variable
in CmdStan's naming (`theta.1`, `Sigma.2.1`) and the sampler diagnostic
columns `lp__`, `accept_stat__`, `stepsize__`, `treedepth__`,
`n_leapfrog__`, `divergent__` and `energy__`. `save_metric` writes the
adapted inverse metric as `metric_file` JSON, and `save_config` the run
configuration. `bayescomp_sample(save_diagnostics = TRUE)` keeps the
unconstrained values, momenta and gradients for CmdStan's
`diagnostic_file`.

### Diagnostic and profile files

A run with `save_diagnostics = TRUE` also writes CmdStan's
`diagnostic_file`, and a program with `profile` blocks writes its
`profile_file`: for each block, the time spent in the block and in the
gradient passing back through it, and the number of gradient evaluations.

```{r}
prof <- bayescomp_model("
data { int N; vector[N] y; vector[N] x; }
parameters { real alpha; real beta; real<lower=0> sigma; }
model {
  profile(\"priors\") { alpha ~ normal(0, 2); beta ~ normal(0, 2); sigma ~ exponential(1); }
  profile(\"likelihood\") { y ~ normal(alpha + beta * x, sigma); }
}", data = list(N = 100, y = 0.5 * x + rnorm(100), x = x))
fit_prof <- bayescomp_sample(prof, chains = 2, iter_warmup = 300, iter_sampling = 300, seed = 1,
                             refresh = 0, save_diagnostics = TRUE)
prof_files <- bayescomp_write_csv(fit_prof, out_dir, basename = "profiled")
list.files(out_dir, "^profiled")
read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "profiled_1_profile.csv"))
```

`bayescomp_read_csv()` reads files written by bayescompR or by CmdStan
itself into a `bayescomp_fit`; with `model`, the unconstrained values are
recovered, so the fit can initialize chains or feed
`bayescomp_generate_quantities()`.

```{r}
fit_csv <- bayescomp_read_csv(files, model = model)
fit_csv
```

## stansummary and diagnose

`bayescomp_stansummary()` prints CmdStan's `stansummary` table, including
the sampler diagnostic rows, ESS per second and timing, from a fit or from
CSV files. `sig_figs`, `percentiles`, `include_param` and `autocorr`
match its options, and `csv_file` writes the table as CSV.

```{r}
bayescomp_stansummary(files, percentiles = c(2.5, 50, 97.5), sig_figs = 3)
```

`bayescomp_diagnose()` runs the checks of CmdStan's `diagnose` program:
tree depth saturation, divergences, E-BFMI (pooled and per chain), low
effective sample size and high R-hat. It also lists proposals that the
sampler rejected because of domain errors or `reject()` calls.

```{r}
d <- bayescomp_diagnose(files)
d$problems
```

## Generated quantities for existing draws

CmdStan's `generate_quantities` method runs the generated quantities
block on draws from an earlier fit, for example after the block was
changed. The new model must have the same parameters.

```{r}
code2 <- sub("real p_mean = inv_logit(alpha);",
             "real p_mean = inv_logit(alpha);\n  array[N] int y_rep = bernoulli_logit_rng(alpha + beta * x);",
             code, fixed = TRUE)
model2 <- bayescomp_model(code2, data = dat)
gq <- bayescomp_generate_quantities(model2, fit_csv, seed = 1)
dim(bayescomp_extract(gq, "y_rep"))
```

The `fit` argument also takes CSV file names, a matrix of parameter draws
with named columns, or a `posterior` draws object.

## The log density and its gradient

`bayescomp_log_prob()` and `bayescomp_grad_log_prob()` evaluate the model
at unconstrained points, as CmdStan's `log_prob` method does, with or
without the Jacobian adjustment and with or without constant terms
(`propto`). `bayescomp_unconstrain()` and `bayescomp_constrain()` convert
between the scales.

```{r}
u <- bayescomp_unconstrain(model, list(alpha = -0.5, beta = 1))
bayescomp_log_prob(model, u)
bayescomp_grad_log_prob(model, u, jacobian = FALSE, propto = TRUE)
```

## Convergence diagnostics for any draws

The diagnostics of the posterior package are also available without it.
Each takes an iterations by chains matrix:

```{r}
mu_draws <- matrix(fit$draws[, , "alpha"], ncol = 2)
c(rhat = bayescomp_rhat(mu_draws), ess_bulk = bayescomp_ess_bulk(mu_draws),
  ess_tail = bayescomp_ess_tail(mu_draws), ess_basic = bayescomp_ess_basic(mu_draws),
  mcse_mean = bayescomp_mcse_mean(mu_draws), mcse_sd = bayescomp_mcse_sd(mu_draws))
bayescomp_ess_quantile(mu_draws, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
```
